cards.text: The writer of Hebrews is writing to believers (Hebrews 3:1), and he just called Jesus a high priest forever in the order of Melchizedek (Hebrews 6:20). This Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He met Abraham, forefather of Israel, coming back from the slaughter of the kings.

cards.question: When Melchizedek and Abraham meet, Abraham blesses Melchizedek.

cards.text: Then Abraham gives Melchizedek a tenth of everything. Friend, when somebody asks me for a tenth of my cookie dough, I need a minute to sit down first.

Then the writer looks at the names: Melchizedek means king of righteousness, and king of Salem means king of peace. Friend, mine just got carved into my handle by the Millers, the family whose kitchen I used to stamp cookies in, so that is a DIFFERENT level of name.
Then the writer describes Melchizedek: without father or mother or genealogy, without beginning of days or end of life. No family tree on file, friend.

cards.question: The writer says Melchizedek remains a priest for all time. Who does he say Melchizedek is like?
The writer says to consider this: even the patriarch Abraham gave Melchizedek a tenth of the plunder. What does that show?

answers.text: How hard the battle had been

cards.text: Now the writer brings in the law. It commands the priests among the sons of Levi, Jacob's son (Genesis 29:34), to collect a tenth from the people, their own brothers, even though the priests come from Abraham too.

cards.question: Melchizedek traces his family line back to Levi.

cards.text: Still, Melchizedek collects a tenth from Abraham and blesses him. Abraham, the man who had the PROMISES, is the one getting blessed, friend.

cards.question: The writer says no one can argue with this: the lesser is blessed by the ___.
Among the Levites, mortal men collect the tenth, but the writer says it is affirmed that Melchizedek lives on.

cards.text: Then the writer says, so to speak, that Levi, the one who COLLECTS the tenth, paid the tenth through Abraham. Friend, that's the toll booth worker paying the toll.

cards.question: When Melchizedek met Abraham, how could Levi pay a tenth through Abraham?

answers.text: Levi was not born yet but came from Abraham
Levi was riding with Abraham's army that day
Levi sent his own tenth along with Abraham

cards.text: Now the writer asks a big question. If perfection could come through the Levitical priesthood, why was another priest still needed, one in the order of Melchizedek and not in the order of Aaron, the priest God set apart (Exodus 28:1)?

cards.question: A priest in the order of Melchizedek still had to come. What does that show about the Levitical priesthood?

answers.text: Perfection could not come through it
It had stopped collecting the tenth
It was never part of the law

cards.text: And here's the thing: the writer says the people received the law on the basis of that priesthood. That priesthood was the ground the law stood on, friend.

cards.question: The writer says that when the priesthood is changed, the ___ must be changed as well.

cards.text: So this new priest the writer's talking about? He belonged to a different tribe, a tribe that has never had anyone serve at the altar.

cards.question: The writer says it is clear which tribe our Lord descended from, a tribe that Moses, Israel's leader, said nothing about priests for. Which tribe?

cards.text: The writer says this point is even MORE clear if another priest like Melchizedek appears. Not just clear, friend. CLEAR clear.

cards.question: The writer says this new priest like Melchizedek became a priest by a law of succession.

cards.text: He became a priest by the power of an INDESTRUCTIBLE life. The writer quotes Psalm 110:4: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”

cards.question: The writer says the former commandment is set aside because it was weak and useless.

cards.text: The writer adds that the law made nothing perfect, and a better hope is introduced. Friend, I'd line up around the block for an upgrade like that.

cards.question: A better hope is introduced. What does the writer say we do by this better hope?

cards.text: Now the writer says none of this happened without an oath. Other priests became priests without one, but Jesus became a priest with an oath.

cards.question: The writer says the Lord swore an oath making Jesus a priest and will not change His mind.

cards.text: Here's the oath, from Psalm 110:4: “The Lord has sworn and will not change His mind: ‘You are a priest forever.’” Friend, I change my mind about sprinkles FOUR times a batch.

cards.question: Because of this oath, what has Jesus become?

answers.text: The guarantee of a better covenant
The keeper of the old law

cards.text: There have been many other priests, because death kept them from continuing in office.

cards.question: The writer says that because Jesus lives forever, His priesthood will someday pass on to another priest.
Jesus is able to save completely those who draw near to God through Him. What reason does the writer give?

answers.text: He always lives to intercede for them
He collects a tenth from each of them
He gives them a new law every day

cards.text: The writer says such a high priest truly befits us: holy, innocent, undefiled, set apart from sinners, and exalted above the heavens. Friend, my résumé has ONE line on it, and it says “stamps cookies.”

cards.question: Unlike the other high priests, Jesus doesn't need to offer daily sacrifices, first for His own sins and then for the people's. How did He sacrifice for sin?

answers.text: Once for all by offering up Himself
Every year on the Day of Atonement
With the blood of bulls and goats

cards.text: Then the writer says the law appoints as high priests men who are weak. I relate, friend, because my edges once went so soft I couldn't stamp a straight line.

cards.question: But the ___, which came after the law, appointed the Son, who has been made perfect forever.
